records.title: Jakarta MRT North–South line
records.answer: Jakarta's North–South MRT combines an operating railway with a staged northern extension. Passenger counts describe use of existing service; civil progress, railway systems and street access describe different steps toward the next opening.
records.scope: One North–South railway across its operating first phase and defined northern extensions, not every line operated or proposed by MRT Jakarta. East–West, Jakarta LRT, Jabodebek LRT and individual station contracts are excluded from this counted identity.
records.stage: The first phase was inaugurated in March 2019. The May 2026 government review retains northern-extension commissioning and opening forecasts for 2027 and 2029. September passenger statistics and traffic notices do not establish a new section's passenger opening.

identity_decision.rationale: Count the named Jakarta North–South MRT railway once across its staged delivery. Do not count individual stations, civil packages or systems contracts again. The separate East–West railway and other Jakarta rail operators are outside this identity. No existing portfolio identity or historical country-acquisition docket is reused.

timeline.event: The embassy's inauguration account dates groundbreaking to this month.
The North–South line inauguration ceremony was held at Bundaran HI.
The indexed operator page dates its package-progress snapshot to this day.
The provincial government described construction progress and future commissioning.
BPS's catalog reports the month's MRT passenger total.
The city published revised traffic arrangements linked to utility constraints.

sections.heading: One railway and several delivery stages
sections.text: The March 24, 2019 ceremony at Bundaran HI marked the North–South line's inauguration after construction that began in October 2013. Japan's embassy describes official development assistance and technical cooperation behind the railway. The counted project remains this named corridor, including its northern extensions, rather than the operator's entire future network. That boundary matters when comparing later announcements: a contract for another line cannot become progress on this one. The inauguration date is also a specific event, not a substitute for the dates when fares, operating hours or subsequent sections changed. Those transitions need their own records.

sections.heading: Passenger use is not a reliability measure
sections.text: BPS's official catalog reports 4,279,584 MRT passengers for September 2026. It lists Jakarta LRT and Transjakarta separately, so combining their totals would change the transport system being described. The MRT figure is a monthly passenger count, not a count of distinct residents or a measurement of trains arriving on time. The underlying statistical release returned an access denial; the catalog excerpt supplies the bounded figure, not the full methodology. Comparing months would require consistent counting rules, service days and any revisions. Crowding, missed transfers and accessible journeys remain different questions from how many passenger movements were recorded.

sections.heading: Northern construction has different package boundaries
sections.text: The operator's indexed February account describes Phase 2A as seven underground stations over roughly 5.8 kilometres, with Phase 2B extending farther north and retaining a feasibility-study stage in that snapshot. Its package table separates civil construction from electrical and mechanical systems, rolling stock and fare collection. A high civil percentage therefore cannot be read as equivalent railway readiness. The May government visit reported overall progress of about 59 percent, a later but differently scoped observation. These dated figures are not November completion measurements. Neither a station count nor a package percentage establishes that an extension can carry passengers safely.

sections.heading: Commissioning and opening need an exact endpoint
sections.text: The May provincial release anticipates commissioning in mid-2027 and gives a late-2027 operating target to Harmoni in the governor's account. Another quotation in the same release names Monas for the 2027 connection; both describe a further extension to Kota in 2029. The different endpoints should not be silently treated as interchangeable. An approved opening scope would need to identify the stations actually entering service and the systems tested together. A future date attached to a broad corridor title does not settle that question. Civil completion, commissioning and permission to carry passengers remain separate decisions with different supporting records.

sections.heading: Utility work changes the streets before opening
sections.text: Central Jakarta's September 9 notice links revised CP201 work timing to utility-network constraints along M.H. Thamrin. It schedules Stage 3B and pedestrian improvements through November 30, with phased changes around the future Thamrin station entrance. The notice assigns the contractor responsibility for motorized and nonmotorized road-user safety. Those arrangements describe how construction is intended to coexist with daily movement, not an observed safe journey or verified restoration. For nearby residents and businesses, the practical outcome includes usable footpaths and crossings throughout the works, not only the eventual railway. A scheduled end date remains different from an actual reopening.

sections.heading: Evidence test from ridership to dependable access
sections.text: Editorial evidence test: keep operating-line passenger data separate from extension delivery, and compare only periods with compatible definitions. Obtain the final opening scope and the integrated tests that bind civil works, power, signalling, trains and station access. Track accessible entrances and transfers as named assets, including outages and recovery, rather than inferring their condition from total ridership. For construction streets, compare promised and actual restoration dates and retain pedestrian access conditions. These steps would connect investment and use to dependable journeys without turning a forecast, ceremony or construction percentage into an operating acceptance.

next_artifacts: Full BPS monthly methodology and consistent revised series when accessible.
Approved opening scope resolving the Harmoni/Monas endpoint distinction.
Integrated systems acceptance and actual passenger-opening records.

records.title: Jakarta–Bandung Whoosh railway
records.answer: Whoosh is an operating intercity railway whose benefits depend on station access as well as train service. Dated accounts distinguish commercial opening, passenger and punctuality periods, ticket-channel changes and unresolved interchange needs.
records.scope: One Jakarta–Bandung high-speed railway operated as Whoosh, not the whole KCIC corporate portfolio or a proposed extension to other cities. Its stations, feeder connections and shuttle services remain components or interfaces, not extra counted projects.
records.stage: Commercial service began October 17, 2023. The 2026 operator reports provide bounded passenger, ticketing and first-half performance observations. November's Padalarang oversight account still seeks access improvements; a new Halim shuttle does not resolve every interchange.

identity_decision.rationale: Count Whoosh once as the named Jakarta–Bandung railway, preserving KCJB as its earlier project name. Stations, feeder trains and connecting shuttle services do not add projects in this group. Bandung city is a separate municipal place, not the whole rail corridor or the regencies containing important station and utility assets.

timeline.event: KCIC's profile dates establishment of the joint venture to this day.
The operator records the railway's inauguration.
The operator records the start of commercial operation.
KCIC published first-half operating indicators and described continuing government coordination.
Parliamentary representatives visited Padalarang; the account was published two days later.
KCIC published January–October digital-ticket figures.
KCIC's November 20 release dates the Halim–BSD–Serpong shuttle start to this day.

sections.heading: Inauguration and paid service are different milestones
sections.text: KCIC's corporate profile dates the railway's inauguration to October 2, 2023 and commercial operation to October 17, following an introductory free-travel period. The Whoosh brand and the earlier Kereta Cepat Jakarta Bandung name describe the same counted railway. They do not create two projects. The profile also recounts the joint venture's formation in October 2015. Its undated financing narrative is historical context, not an audited statement of today's debt allocation or public exposure. A clear account of the railway can establish that passenger service exists while leaving financial restructuring and any later expansion to their own dated evidence.

sections.heading: Operating figures retain their reporting periods
sections.text: KCIC's August 6 statement reports 99.4 percent punctuality and 95.79 percent customer satisfaction for the first half of 2026. These are operator-reported indicators, not an independent guarantee for every subsequent trip. Its more-than-16.9-million passenger figure is cumulative through July, rather than a January–July total. The same statement describes continuing coordination with Danantara and the finance ministry while service continues. That distinction matters: operating trains and settled financing are not the same condition. Assessing sustained performance requires the punctuality threshold, treatment of cancellations and survey method, with financial outcomes evaluated from their own records.

sections.heading: Digital ticketing changes a transaction rather than a whole footprint
sections.text: The November 17 release reports about 3.9 million digital-ticket users within about 5.1 million passengers during January–October, retaining the stated 75.9 percent share. KCIC estimates roughly Rp5.8 billion in potential avoided printing cost using Rp1,500 per paper ticket. This is a ticket-material comparison, not audited net profit or a lifecycle emissions result for the railway. The release also retains machines, staffed assistance for passengers with particular needs and mobile staff helping online transactions. A high digital share does not establish universal digital access. The useful service question is whether people can complete purchase and boarding through a channel they can use.

sections.heading: Padalarang exposes the importance of the onward journey
sections.text: A parliamentary account published November 15 describes a November 13 visit to Padalarang and concerns about narrow access, congested pick-up space and feeder coordination. Participants said a direct access connection agreed in August 2025 remained in planning. Those are attributed oversight findings, not a newly measured congestion series or proof that an improvement has opened. The committee requested clearer responsibilities, schedules and financing for the surrounding interchange. The lesson is specific: a fast intercity train can still deliver an inconvenient whole journey when access roads and connecting services do not work together. Train speed alone cannot measure that experience.

sections.heading: Halim gains a connecting service with limited initial capacity
sections.text: KCIC's November 20 announcement dates a direct shuttle between Halim, BSD and Serpong to November 18. It describes three departures in each direction daily and fourteen seats per departure during the initial service. These are offered capacity and frequency, not observed occupancy or a guaranteed connection with every train. The addition broadens onward options at Halim, but it does not settle the separate Padalarang access issues. A passenger still needs compatible departure times, a usable boarding point and an available seat. Service announcements therefore belong beside connection conditions rather than being presented as complete door-to-door reliability.

sections.heading: Evidence test for an operating intercity railway
sections.text: Editorial evidence test: evaluate the train and its connections over the same travel periods while preserving their separate operators and responsibilities. Obtain punctuality definitions, cancellations and recovery records, then examine transfer waiting time and accessible boarding at named interchanges. Compare ticket-channel savings with the costs and support needed to provide those channels. Follow access-road commitments to actual completion, rather than counting a planning agreement as a delivered improvement. Keep audited finance and any extension approval separate from passenger totals. This would show where an operating railway produces dependable journeys and where the next investment or service correction is needed.

next_artifacts: Defined punctuality and cancellation series plus customer-survey methods.
Dated Padalarang access responsibilities, financing and accepted works.
Observed feeder and shuttle connections including accessible boarding.
Current audited financial and restructuring records, separate from service use.

records.title: Bandung municipal services
records.answer: Bandung's water and waste systems extend across municipal boundaries, while service access remains local. Supply expansion, water-loss targets, maintenance notices, wastewater treatment and proposed neighbourhood composting need different measures of delivery.
records.scope: One Kota Bandung municipality, not Kabupaten Bandung, Bandung Barat, Cimahi or the entire metropolitan area. External treatment and transport dependencies are described without annexing their locations or counting component facilities as additional projects.
records.stage: The 2026 water-strategy catalog, utility program descriptions and maintenance notices establish distinct policy and service arrangements. November composting plans still concern future work. No city-wide continuous-supply, wastewater-compliance or waste-diversion outcome is admitted.

identity_decision.rationale: Count Kota Bandung once within its municipal boundary. Keep Bojongsoang's location in Bandung regency and wider rail, intake and disposal dependencies explicit without enlarging the place. Gedebage, northern water-loss work and neighbourhood composting are service examples rather than additional project or place identities in this group.

timeline.event: The utility dates Bojongsoang wastewater treatment operation to this year.
The northern water-loss program reports its 45.79% baseline for this year.
The municipal catalog dates adoption and promulgation of the water strategy to this day.
The catalog lists this as publication of its water-strategy record.
Tirtawening published a planned production interruption linked to Pakar maintenance.
The mayor announced proposed neighbourhood compost pits, reported November 9.
The utility published non-piped water and wastewater service channels.

sections.heading: Water strategy and eastern supply expansion
sections.text: Bandung's legal catalog lists Regulation 9/2026 for the 2026–2030 drinking-water strategy, adopted and promulgated February 11 and published in the catalog March 12. This establishes a dated policy record, not delivery to every household. Tirtawening's separate Gedebage description connects eastern service areas to Cikalong intake and treatment through transmission and distribution. Its bounded service-area population is not an active-connection count. The undated account describes completion work rather than verified continuous supply. For residents, the distinction is practical: a planned network and an application channel do not by themselves show that usable water reaches a particular home.

sections.heading: Reducing water losses needs a consistent baseline
sections.text: The northern-area program reports non-revenue water of 45.79 percent in 2020 and an eleven-year target of 17 percent under a performance-based arrangement. The target is not a current measured result, and the page does not supply an exact start date for calculating its deadline. It describes district metering, active leak control, commercial-loss recovery and network restructuring. These interventions address different reasons why supplied water does not become billed consumption. A fall in the combined percentage needs interpretation alongside input volumes, meters and service coverage. Potential coverage gains cannot be counted as households already receiving reliable water.

sections.heading: Maintenance connects water supply with energy infrastructure
sections.text: A September 21 notice planned a roughly sixteen-hour halt at Mini Plant Dago Pakar while the shared Pakar daily storage and hydropower intake arrangement underwent maintenance. It anticipated a 400-litre-per-second production reduction and identified service areas potentially affected. These are planned effects, not a record of actual interruption length or confirmed restoration at household taps. November's separate non-piped service notice provides channels for tanker water and wastewater removal, but not response-time or capacity results. Together they show why resilience depends on both the main system and workable alternatives, with delivery and restoration assessed at the customer end.

sections.heading: Wastewater crosses the municipal boundary
sections.text: Tirtawening locates the Bojongsoang treatment works in Bandung regency, although it treats household wastewater from Bandung city. Its account dates operation to 1992 and describes stabilization ponds, treated-water uses and residual streams. That external location does not expand the counted municipality. It does make service dependencies visible: collecting wastewater, conveying it to treatment and managing screenings, sludge and effluent involve more than a city-boundary map. The utility's general description of safe effluent is not a current laboratory compliance record. Nor does the plant's existence establish that every city household is connected to the sewer system.

sections.heading: Neighbourhood composting is a proposal with local operating needs
sections.text: A municipal account published November 9 reports the mayor's November 6 proposal for three compost pits in each RW, a neighbourhood administrative unit, with work intended to start the following month. The stated 1,597 RW denominator describes the program's intended reach, not completed coverage. Training would pass through local administrations to neighbourhood groups. At the November 22 inspection, the proposed December start was still future. Installed pits would also need suitable separated material, routine operation and a use for finished compost. A construction count alone would not demonstrate sustained waste diversion or reduced disposal pressure.

sections.heading: Evidence test from facilities to household service
sections.text: Editorial evidence test: map each service's actual customer boundary separately from the municipality and the location of its assets. For water, follow connection status, supply hours, pressure, quality and restoration after interruptions. For loss reduction, retain the baseline method and distinguish physical from commercial recovery. For wastewater, connect collection coverage to dated influent, effluent and residual-handling results. For composting, record functioning sites, material quality and quantities processed over comparable periods. These measures would make the relationship between plans and daily services testable without treating a facility, target or contact number as a completed city-wide outcome.

next_artifacts: Dated active connections, supply continuity and water-quality observations by service area.
Comparable northern water-loss results and contract-period definitions.
Actual outage restoration and non-piped response records.
Wastewater sampling/coverage and functioning compost-site throughput.
